title: Apps & installing
blurb: Installing and removing apps, Store problems, apps that won't start.

remedies.title: Adobe Acrobat or Reader problems (sign-in, crashes, protected mode)
remedies.why: Acrobat needs sign-in for licences, and its Protected Mode can clash with some setups.

steps.text: Help › Check for Updates; Help › Repair Installation (Windows).
Edit › Preferences › Security (Enhanced) › turn off Protected Mode at startup, if PDFs won't open at all (turn back on later).
Sign out and in via Help or the Creative Cloud app for licence errors.
For everyday PDF jobs offline, DeskFolio is a free alternative.

remedies.title: An app says Java is missing or the wrong version
remedies.why: Older business apps need a Java runtime installed.

steps.text: Install the Java version the app's maker names (often an OpenJDK build like Eclipse Temurin).
Uninstall old Java versions you don't need; they're a security risk.

remedies.escalate: Work apps: IT usually packages the right Java.

remedies.title: An app says it needs permission (Accessibility, Full Disk Access, Screen Recording)
remedies.why: macOS asks you to approve apps that control the computer, read protected folders or record the screen.

steps.text: Privacy & Security › the category the app names › turn it on (unlock with your password).
Quit and reopen the app afterwards.
If it's already on but still asks, turn it off and on, or remove it with − and add again.

remedies.title: App says it doesn't support this Mac, or needs Rosetta
symptoms: app not supported on this mac
remedies.why: Some apps are built only for Intel Macs; Rosetta lets them run on Apple silicon.

steps.text: Accept the prompt to install Rosetta when it appears.
Download the Apple silicon (or Universal) version from the maker if there is one.

remedies.title: An app keeps asking to update (or won't update)
remedies.why: The updater lacks rights, the app is open, or a copy in another folder is the one running.

steps.text: Quit the app fully and run its update again.
Download the latest installer from the maker and install over it.
Check you don't have two copies (e.g. in Downloads and Applications).

remedies.title: Install common apps safely (without dodgy download sites)
remedies.why: Download sites often bundle adware; the Store or the maker's site are safe.

steps.text: Use the Microsoft Store, the maker's own website, or winget (e.g. winget install Mozilla.Firefox in Terminal).
Avoid "free download" sites and ads that look like download buttons.

remedies.title: An old app looks blurry or tiny on a high-resolution screen
remedies.why: Older apps don't understand display scaling.

steps.text: Right-click the app's shortcut › Properties › Compatibility › Change high DPI settings › Override high DPI scaling: System (Enhanced).
Turn on "Let Windows try to fix apps so they're not blurry" in Display › Scale.
